laboratoryGuardrails.name: sample-snapshot-immutability
laboratoryGuardrails.description: A collected sample retains an immutable authoritative physiological source snapshot across later treatment, physiology, restart and takeover changes.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: result-uses-sample-time
laboratoryGuardrails.description: A released result represents physiology at sampledAt rather than resultAvailableAt.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: exactly-once-order-sample-result
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Retry, reconnect, restart, rerender and takeover cannot duplicate an order, sample, result or result-group release.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: single-writer-authority
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Only authoritative Runtime authority advances laboratory state. Readers use supported durable commands and never generate authoritative results locally.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: reader-convergence
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Readers converge on the same order, sample time, availability time, result payload and status without local result generation.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: restart-takeover-determinism
laboratoryGuardrails.description: A persisted sample produces the same result after app, writer or reader restart and writer takeover, without rerandomization or later-state recomputation.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: timing-persistence
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Configured result availability remains anchored to sample time and countdowns do not reset during restart or takeover.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: no-early-release
laboratoryGuardrails.description: No result group reaches RESULTED before its configured availability time.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: independent-result-groups
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Releasing one result group neither releases another group early nor changes any group's sample snapshot.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: terminal-fencing
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Terminal exercise fencing prevents new laboratory progression, result generation, prohibited pending release and workflow resurrection.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: package-scope
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Laboratory exposure remains limited to the frozen EMO trauma and IRO package scopes.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: ab0-identity-stability
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Patient AB0 and RhD identity remains stable across repeated sampling, restart and takeover.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: dynamic-physiology-source-of-truth
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Dynamic results derive from authoritative physiology and state rather than UI-local calculations.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: mtp-ica-coherence
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Dynamic ionized calcium and the MTP calcium recommendation remain distinct mechanisms without hard-coded substitution in either direction.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: no-resulted-sample-recalculation
laboratoryGuardrails.description: A RESULTED sample and payload are immutable and cannot be regenerated from current physiology.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: canonical-persistence
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Laboratory persistence forbids reader-local revisions, restores deterministically and gives authoritative persisted state precedence without semantic drift.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: stable-action-identity-under-rehydration
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Checkpoint rehydration, rerender, reconnect and projection replacement cannot change an in-progress laboratory gesture from ORDER to COLLECT or COLLECT to ORDER, or create duplicate durable commands.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: latched-lab-action-intent
laboratoryGuardrails.description: A physical laboratory gesture latches ORDER or COLLECT at press-in; rehydration may invalidate and abort that action but can never substitute the other durable command.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: valid-lab-gesture-reaches-durable-submit
laboratoryGuardrails.description: An action valid at gesture start attempts exactly one durable submission despite stale checkpoint or projection rehydration; only a provably newer incompatible authoritative state may abort it.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: physical-lab-press-delivery-survives-rehydration
laboratoryGuardrails.description: A visible enabled laboratory action retains stable mounted native touch-target identity across ordinary rehydration so a physical gesture reaches press-in and exactly one latched durable submission or an explicit newer-authority invalidation; silent gesture loss is forbidden.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: lab-action-enablement-requires-command-ready-reader-state
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Laboratory ORDER and COLLECT controls are enabled only while the shared durable patient-command path is ready; checkpoint reconciliation disables the stable semantic control until readiness returns automatically.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: result-release-after-threshold-crossing
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Authoritative simulation-time progression releases every due non-terminal result group exactly once when time reaches or crosses availableAt, including large jumps, restart, takeover and later supported steps.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: complete-polytrauma-package
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Every source-supported reportable POLÜTRAUMA component is represented and explicit Narva exclusions remain absent.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: deterministic-static-generation
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Static baseline analytes are deterministic for the same patient and immutable sample snapshot without random, wall-clock, device or reader-local inputs.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: scenario-derived-result-stability
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Explicit authoritative sample-time scenario overrides win only for supported static analytes and remain stable after later scenario change.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: blood-bank-identity-persistence
laboratoryGuardrails.description: AB0, RhD and antibody-screen identity remains patient-stable across samples, restart, takeover and rehydration.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: hcg-applicability
laboratoryGuardrails.description: hCG is reported only when an authoritative patient applicability fact exists; missing demographic evidence is not converted into an invented result.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: narva-package-exclusions
laboratoryGuardrails.description: SARS-CoV-2, influenza, urine analyses and U-Narco remain absent from the Narva POLÜTRAUMA result.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: complete-cbc-coverage
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Hematology contains every authoritative IVKH CBC/5-diff/NRBC component while Hb, Hct and platelets remain physiology-driven.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: source-unit-reference-fidelity
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Source codes, units, references, conditionality and explicit ambiguities are preserved where authoritative metadata exists and missing metadata is not invented.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: static-scenario-sample-immutability
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Static, demographic, blood-bank and scenario-derived results use only immutable sample-time state and cannot change after later treatment or progression.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: static-restart-takeover-determinism
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Pending and released B31 results survive restart and produce identical payloads through writer takeover without regeneration drift.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: reader-restriction-for-static-results
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Readers may display persisted B31 payloads but cannot generate, revise or release them locally.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: independent-complete-result-groups
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Astrup, hematology, blood bank, clinical chemistry and coagulation retain independent sampledAt-anchored release boundaries after complete package generation.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: complete-result-ui-reachability
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Every canonical reportable result remains reachable in the laboratory presentation without silent omission.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: deterministic-result-group-order
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Laboratory result groups render in canonical package order across rerender, rehydration and restart.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: deterministic-analyte-order
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Analytes render in canonical catalog order within their result group, independent of payload transport order.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: valid-reference-abnormal-flags
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Numeric LOW, HIGH and normal presentation flags derive only from one valid authoritative numeric reference range and include non-color semantics.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: no-invented-abnormal-flag
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Missing, qualitative, demographic-ambiguous or source-ambiguous reference metadata never produces an invented abnormal flag.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: qualitative-result-presentation
laboratoryGuardrails.description: AB0, RhD, antibody screen and other canonical qualitative values render as qualitative results rather than malformed numeric values.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: hcg-presentation-applicability
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Canonical hCG results render only when applicable; not-applicable state never displays a fabricated numeric value.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: source-ambiguous-presentation
laboratoryGuardrails.description: SOURCE_AMBIGUOUS components remain explicitly unresolved and cannot be mistaken for completed measurements.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: pending-result-group-presentation
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Processing groups remain visibly pending without fake values and transition once to their canonical released result.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: stable-result-row-identity
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Group and analyte presentation keys derive from stable canonical identities rather than revisions, indexes or render order.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: result-presentation-rehydration-consistency
laboratoryGuardrails.description: The same canonical result renders identically after rerender and checkpoint rehydration without duplicates or ordering drift.

laboratoryGuardrails.name: result-presentation-canonical-immutability
laboratoryGuardrails.description: Presentation grouping, ordering, expansion and abnormal classification never mutate the canonical laboratory payload.
